newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay bourse to set up bank to fund brokers.
newsitem.headline: Bombay bourse to set up bank to fund brokers.

text.p: Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) president M.G. Damani said on Wednesday the exchange would soon set up a bank to provide funds to stock brokers, the United News of India (UNI) reported.
UNI said the bank, to be promoted by BSE stock brokers, would cater to their investment and financial needs.
The stock market watchdog Securities and Exchange Board of India had already initiated the process of setting up the bank, UNI said.
"Sooner than later we will have a bank of our own," it quoted Damani as saying.
Brokers in India are generally short of funds and conservative banks do not lend them money.
"Now, with this bank in place, the brokers will not have to go anywhere for money for their investments," Damani said.
UNI quoted Damani as saying that the bank would initially be set up as a cooperative society which would provide funds to its member brokers and later transform itself into a bank.
"In the second phase we will enroll brokers and in the third phase we intend to enroll the investors," Damani said.
Damani said private parties or bank could be permitted to hold stakes in the bank, which in its initial stages would provide services like money transfers and advances against shares.
Damani said the bank expected to break even in the first year of operations.
